enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **f)** Discuss the importance of trees to man.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: trees are among the most valuable gifts of nature.
2. Oxygen, clean air and shade.
3. Food, wood and income.
4. Medicine, protection of the soil and the climate.
5. The danger of cutting trees carelessly, what we should do, conclusion.

**Model composition (464 words)**

Trees are among the most valuable gifts that nature has given to man. Without them, life on earth would be difficult, if not impossible. They give us food, shelter, medicine and clean air, and they protect the environment in which we live.

First, trees provide the oxygen which we breathe. During the day, their leaves take in carbon dioxide, which we breathe out and which factories and vehicles release into the air, and they give out oxygen. A town with many trees therefore has fresher air than one without them. Trees also give shade, and a person who rests under a mango tree on a hot afternoon knows how pleasant it is.

Second, trees supply food. Mango, orange, pear, avocado, coconut and many other fruits come from trees, and people eat them or sell them to earn money. Cocoa and coffee, which grow best in shade, bring income to thousands of Cameroonian farmers. Honey, which bees make from the flowers of trees, is also a source of food and money.

Third, trees provide wood. Carpenters use timber to make doors, tables, beds and chairs, builders use it for roofs, and most rural families cook with firewood. The timber industry also gives employment to many young people and brings foreign currency to the country.

Fourth, trees give medicine. The bark, roots and leaves of many trees are used in traditional medicine to treat malaria, stomach pain and coughs, and those who sell herbal remedies earn their living from the forest. Some modern drugs were also first discovered from the extracts of trees.

Fifth, trees protect the soil and the climate. Their roots hold the earth together and prevent erosion and landslides during heavy rains. They release water vapour into the air, which helps to bring rain, and they reduce the heat of the sun. Where trees have been cut down, the land becomes dry and the desert slowly advances.

Sixth, trees beautify our surroundings and shelter animals. Birds, monkeys and insects live in trees, and a green avenue or park makes a town pleasant to live in. Tourists also travel long distances to see forests and national parks, and they spend money which helps the economy.

In spite of all these benefits, man continues to cut down trees carelessly for farms, firewood and charcoal, and he sets bushes on fire during the dry season. The result is floods, drought and global warming. We must therefore plant a tree whenever we cut one down, and the government should punish those who destroy forests illegally. Schools can also create tree-planting clubs.

In conclusion, trees are the friends of man. If we protect them, they will protect us, and future generations will also enjoy their gifts. Let each of us therefore plant at least one tree every year.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Listing uses of trees in one paragraph with no development: each use needs an explanation and an example, in its own paragraph.
2. Forgetting to discuss (the verb of the topic): a good answer also mentions the threats to trees and what man should do.
